key_insight: Local splitting and merging in disordered pore networks gives rise to a Gamma-distributed pore-body flow rate, which in turn determines the pore-throat flow statistics.
engineering_relevance: The model enables fast prediction of flow-rate distributions in porous media from minimal geometric information, improving design and analysis of filtration, transport, and subsurface flow systems.
method: Steady Stokes flow is studied in 2D disordered arrays of circular obstacles.
A pore-network model is built to capture local flow correlations between connected pores.
The Gamma distribution is parameterized from simple geometry, especially the coefficient of variation of pore-throat widths.
evidence_signal: The predictions agree closely with computational fluid dynamics simulations and outperform prior mean-field models that ignore local flow-rate correlations.
watch_item: The theory is developed for steady Stokes flow in two-dimensional disordered media, so extension to 3D, inertial effects, or strongly heterogeneous geometries may require revalidation.
paper_title: Topological origin of flow distributions in disordered porous media
